title: Why your brain begs for one more scroll

scenes.visual: Big hook text, curious Norb peeking from below
Phone with endlessly scrolling feed cards; Norb watches hooked
scenes.voiceover: Every swipe is a tiny lottery. Most posts are boring, but the next one might be amazing.

scenes.visual: Reward sparkles burst around the dopamine character; Norb gets jittery
scenes.voiceover: That maybe fires dopamine. Your brain rewards the chance, not the post.

scenes.visual: Three dots chase each other around a circle, never arriving; Norb exhausted
scenes.voiceover: So you chase the next maybe, and the next. A loop with no finish line.

scenes.visual: Navy friction wall with a lock pops up and blocks the lunging phone; Norb gets the idea
scenes.voiceover: The way out is not willpower. It is friction: make scrolling cost an extra step.

scenes.visual: THE SCIENCE card; below it a bar chart of dopamine vs reward chance pops up, peaking and sparkling at 50% 'maybe'; Norb curious
scenes.voiceover:
Dopamine peaks when a reward is a maybe, not a sure thing.
The slot machine trick: a variable reward schedule.

scenes.visual: TRY THIS card; below it the coral app icon gets dragged off the phone and tossed away; Norb celebrates
scenes.voiceover:
Log out after every use.
Move the app off your home screen.
